context: Neonatal Conjunctivitis › 3.12.2 · sticky eyes vs ophthalmia neonatorum › Treat the parents
fragment: Also treat the mother and her partner for sexually transmitted infections: ceftriaxone 500 mg IM as a single dose for gonorrhoea (amoxicillin and spectinomycin are no longer adequate), plus doxycycline for Chlamydia unless it has been excluded. Refer to the STI control guidelines.

context: Congenital Syphilis › 3.13.1 · snuffles, rash, penicillin › Treatment
fragment: Asymptomatic neonates born to women with a positive VDRL or rapid plasma reagin test (with a normal evaluation): benzathine benzylpenicillin 50 000 U/kg (≈ 37.5 mg/kg) as a single IM dose.

context: Congenital Syphilis › 3.13.1 · snuffles, rash, penicillin › Treatment
fragment: Symptomatic infants — preferred: aqueous crystalline penicillin G 100 000–150 000 U/kg/day IV (50 000 U/kg every 12 h for the first 7 days, then every 8 h to complete 10 days). Where IV is not feasible: procaine benzylpenicillin 50 mg/kg as a single deep IM dose daily for 10 days.

context: Severe Anaemia › 7.5.2 · transfuse slowly · 20 ml/kg › Monitoring
fragment: If there are basal lung crepitations or an enlarging liver, STOP the transfusion and give furosemide 1 mg/kg IV. Re-transfusion: rather than a rigid "no repeat within 4 days" rule, monitor Hb serially (~8 h, 24 h and day 3–4) and re-transfuse based on clinical status and Hb trajectory. Avoid unnecessary repeat transfusions — preferring whole blood reduces the need for a second transfusion.

context: Continuing Diarrhoea › 7.5.4 · giardia · cryptosporidium · lactose › Giardiasis
fragment: Examine the stools by microscopy where possible. If cysts or trophozoites of Giardia lamblia are found, give metronidazole 7.5 mg/kg every 8 h for 7 days.
